University Staff**Description**
---------------

 **University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus**

**Department: Medicine – Division of Transplant Medicine**

**Job Title: Finance Program Manager**

**Position \#: 00853028 – Requisition \#: 41046**

 **Job Summary:**

  

This is an excellent opportunity for a finance professional who enjoys using data, analysis, and partnership to support meaningful work in academic medicine. The Finance Program Manager will serve as the primary financial reporting and analysis resource for the Division of Transplant Medicine, the first division of its kind in the United States, while also providing financial reporting and analytical support for the Division of Hospital Medicine. In this role, the successful candidate will help translate complex financial and operational information into clear, actionable insights that support clinical operations, faculty planning, budgeting, forecasting, and long\-term strategic decision\-making.

  

The position offers broad exposure to financial reporting, provider productivity, clinical revenue, business case development, and process improvement in a dynamic, mission\-driven environment. Day to day, this individual will build and maintain financial models, monitor key performance trends, partner with division and department leaders, and identify opportunities to strengthen reporting workflows, improve revenue capture, and support responsible stewardship of divisional resources. For someone who is detail\-oriented, collaborative, and interested in making a visible impact, this role provides the opportunity to contribute directly to the growth and success of an innovative clinical and academic enterprise.

 **Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead financial reporting and analysis for the Division of Transplant Medicine, including provider productivity, clinical activity, wRVU performance, cFTE targets, monthly financial results, and other key financial and operational metrics, while providing monthly financial reporting and related analytical support for the Division of Hospital Medicine.
* Monitor financial performance, identify trends and variances, and provide timely analyses and recommendations to support operational and strategic decision\-making.
* Develop and maintain financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, business case development, faculty recruitment, compensation planning, clinical initiatives, and long\-range planning.
* Support day\-to\-day management and oversight of divisional funds, including clinical, grant, gift, and other funding sources, ensuring appropriate use, documentation, reconciliation, and reporting.
* Partner with division leadership, the Department of Medicine finance team, CU Medicine, and other stakeholders to resolve financial questions, improve reporting workflows, and strengthen alignment with institutional requirements.
* Ensure CU Medicine sites of practice and related billing information are accurate, current, and aligned with division clinical operations and provider assignments.
* Provide guidance on procurement, reimbursement, payment activities, fund selection, and related compliance requirements to ensure transactions are accurate, allowable, properly documented, and aligned with applicable policies.
 **Work Location:**

  

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 3 days per week on campus and as needed for in\-person meetings.

 **Why Join Us:**

  

The CU Anschutz Division of Transplant Medicine is the newest division in the Department of Medicine, formed to bring together world\-class experts dedicated to advancing patient care, groundbreaking research and educating future transplant leaders. The first division of its kind in the United States, we serve as a hub for interdisciplinary collaboration, driving new discoveries and improving outcomes for transplant recipients. Our faculty represent some of the nation’s leading transplant clinicians, scientists, and educators, united by a shared commitment to excellence and innovation.

 **Why work for the University?**

 **Minimum Qualifications:**

jobs.title: Case Manager
jobs.description:
**Case Manager \- PHAP**

**Peer Assistance Services, Inc.** is a community\-based, 501(c)(3\), non\-for\-profit Colorado corporation. Our mission, to lead with prevention and intervention for substance use and mental health concerns, guides all agency programming. Our values of grit, integrity, and compassion are guideposts for all that we do in the service of our mission. Each staff member operates from these to ensure the success of the agency. PAS implements two statewide programs, Screening Brief Intervention, Referral to treatment (SBIRT), and the Peer Health Assistance Programs (PHAP)

**Screening, Brief, Intervention, and Referral to Treatment, or SBIRT,** is an evidence\-based early intervention practice to identify, reduce, and prevent use of alcohol and other substances. SBIRT calls for community\-based screening for health risk behaviors, including substance use. SBIRT in Colorado is a statewide program that provides training, technical assistance, and implementation support to health and mental healthcare providers, healthcare organizations, and stakeholders. SBIRT in Colorado manages a statewide campaign to increase public awareness of the risks related to alcohol, marijuana, and other drug use and to reduce the stigma of seeking treatment.

**Peer Health Assistance Programs** contract with the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies, Division of Professions and Occupations to provide the Peer Health Assistance Programs which are statutorily created and funded by license fees. These programs provide assessment, referral, long\-term case management and monitoring for health and mental health professionals with physical, emotional, psychiatric, psychological and/or substance use conditions affecting their practice.


These are the professions who have statutorily created programs for Nurses – RNs and LPNs, Direct Entry Midwives, Dentists and Dental Hygienists, Pharmacists and Pharmacy Interns, Veterinary Professionals, Marriage and Family Therapists, Professional Counselors, Psychologists, Social Workers, Addiction Counselors, and Unlicensed Psychotherapists.


The Peer Health Assistance Program is available on a fee for service basis to other licensed healthcare providers in Colorado who do not have a statutorily created program. These professions include physical therapists, surgical technicians/assistants, chiropractors, optometrists, nursing home administrators, podiatrists, athletic trainers, massage therapists, occupational therapists, respiratory therapists, and speech and language pathologists.  

Please visit our website at https://www.peerassistanceservices.org/ to learn more about the agency.

**About the Case Manager Position**


This is a hands\-on, full\-time position with day\-to\-day responsibilities that will include ensuring program participants are able to practice their profession with reasonable skill and safety, while complying with regulatory requirements. You will also collaborate with licensed evaluators to develop a monitoring contract outlining treatment and community resources to optimize program participants' physical and mental health and wellbeing. You will need to maintain regular communication with program participants, treatment providers, and workplace supervisors to measure compliance with the monitoring contract. You may also have to adjust monitoring contract requirements based on compliance measurements while keeping accurate records of contract monitoring throughout the program participant's involvement in the Peer Health Assistance Program. Your goal will be to help program participants achieve optimal health and well\-being while also meeting regulatory requirements.

**Compensation:** $55,000 to $60,000

**What will you do?**

* Provides comprehensive case management for Peer Health program participants.
* Comprehensive management of compliance with monitoring contracts.
* Collaborates with licensed clinical evaluators to provide referrals to treatment and other resources.
* Maintains accurate electronic participant records.
* Communicates with State Regulatory Boards.
* Directs participants to appropriate providers.
* Establishes and manages relationships with key partners, e.g., treatment and healthcare providers, employers, supervisors, and practice monitors.
* Conducts regular audits of program participants for quality assurance.
* Attends staff meetings including clinical consultation, office hours, case review, required trainings, and all agency meetings.
* Assists with additional program activities as requested.

**What education \& experience is required in this role?**

* Bachelor’s degree in a health and behavioral health\-related field, e.g., nursing, social work, or human services, is required.
* Two or more years of experience in case management is preferred.

**Do you have these special skills?**

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Attention to detail and organization skills.
* Deliver high\-quality services to program participants and contracts.
* critical thinking

**Closing Date: applications are accepted on an ongoing basis**  

  

Colorado Residents: In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age\-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information. **What makes us different?**


* Comprehensive Medical (United HealthCare), Dental, and Vision.

* Retirement plan option \- 403(b)(7\) for eligible employees
* Generous Flexible Time Off (FTO)
* Part\-time, paid sick leave accrual, but not eligible for FTO employees.

**Essential Functions:**


*Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.*



The **Traffic Control Supervisor** oversees operations related to traffic control including road and highway construction projects. The Traffic Control Supervisor is responsible for setting up and maintaining temporary traffic control in work zones. Their duties include using traffic control devices to divert drivers and pedestrians, monitoring road repairs, and supervising teams as they install equipment. Responsibilities are to employ traffic control devices to divert pedestrians and drivers, monitor the repair of roads, and supervise teams as they install equipment. * Perform a needs assessment when speaking with customers to translate their requests into our related products
* Maintain delivery/pickup tickets.
* Learn/Responsible for safe lifting, loading, unloading of equipment to and from trucks.
* Keep company vehicles clean and orderly, informing management of any safety concerns or vehicle problems.
* Arrive to work site on time wearing proper Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), e.g., hard hats, safety shoes, safety glasses, gloves, masks, and earplugs as required, and when applicable, a respirator.
* Adhere to all Company Policies and Procedures.
* Direct traffic at construction sites to ensure the safety of workers, pedestrians, and motorists.
* Set up and maintain traffic control devices such as cones, signs, and barricades.
* Communicate effectively with construction crews to coordinate traffic control efforts.
* Monitor traffic patterns and adjust control measures as needed.
* Report any incidents or issues to supervisors promptly.

The Social Worker (MSW) is responsible for non\-clinical, biopsychosocial assessments and interventions for the inpatient floors and the outpatient emergency department. The MSW performs crisis intervention, patient/family interventions, high\-risk screening, focused emotional support, and referrals for financial assistance or other identified resource needs. The MSW assists in post\-acute care placement on all discharges, primarily with those patients identified with post\-discharge behavioral health and patient assistance/resource needs. The MSW is dedicated to patient and family\-centered care that values personal self\-determination, prioritization, and engages in creative and compassionate problem\-solving. The MSW responds to physician, non\-discharge planning social work consults throughout the facility.

* You will work collaboratively with RN case managers, acute care nurses, physicians, insurance companies, and other staff members to proactively identify and address patient needs.

* You will maintain a thorough working knowledge of the rules of Medicare, Medicaid, and private payer regulations and processes. You will possess a thorough understanding of managed\-care concepts and length\-of\-stay management relating to patient and organizational fiscal responsibility.

jobs.description:
Job Overview  
We are seeking a dedicated and compassionate Licensed Clinical Professional Counselor (LCPC) to join our dynamic mental health team. In this vital role, you will provide comprehensive psychotherapy and mental health services to diverse populations, including adults. Your expertise will help clients navigate complex emotional, behavioral, and psychological challenges, fostering resilience and promoting overall well\-being. As an LCPC, you will utilize evidence\-based practices and innovative treatment modalities to deliver personalized care through telehealth platforms. Your commitment to ethical standards and client\-centered approaches will make a meaningful difference in the lives of those you serve.

Responsibilities

* Conduct thorough mental health assessments and clinical evaluations using ICD\-9 and ICD\-10 coding standards to determine client needs.
* Develop individualized treatment plans incorporating evidence\-based practices such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), trauma\-focused therapy, psychodynamic therapy, and behavioral therapy.
* Provide individual, group, family, and child/youth counseling sessions utilizing techniques like motivational interviewing, grief counseling, art therapy, dance/movement therapy, and social work strategies.
* Manage crisis situations effectively through crisis intervention, crisis management protocols, and trauma\-informed care to ensure client safety.
* Maintain accurate clinical documentation adhering to HIPAA regulations, medical documentation standards, and clinical ethical guidelines within electronic health records (EHR/EMR).
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams on case management, medical records review, and patient care coordination for clients with co\-occurring disorders or developmental disabilities.
* Engage in ongoing research and data collection to enhance clinical practices and contribute to quality improvement initiatives.

Requirements

* Valid licensure as a Licensed Clinical Professional Counselor (LCPC) or equivalent in the applicable state or region.
* Proven experience working with adolescents, individuals with disabilities—including autism—and diverse populations such as geriatrics or pediatrics.
* Strong knowledge of psychotherapeutic modalities including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), psychodynamic therapy, trauma\-focused therapy, addiction counseling, and behavior management techniques.
* Experience working with individuals with co\-occurring disorders or complex mental health needs such as PTSD or chronic pain management.
* Proficiency in clinical documentation standards, ICD coding (ICD\-9/ICD\-10\), medical terminology, and telehealth therapy platforms.
* Ability to perform mental health assessments accurately using diagnostic tools aligned with HIPAA guidelines.
* Excellent communication skills for client engagement and collaboration with healthcare teams; experience in inpatient or outpatient settings is preferred.
* Commitment to ethical practice standards and ongoing professional development in behavioral health.

Join our team to make a lasting impact by providing compassionate care rooted in evidence\-based practices! We value energetic professionals who are eager to support clients’ mental health journeys through innovative therapies and collaborative approaches. Your expertise will help foster healthier communities while advancing your career in a supportive environment dedicated to excellence in clinical care.

**Case Manager \- PHAP**

**Peer Assistance Services, Inc.** is a community\-based, 501(c)(3\), non\-for\-profit Colorado corporation. Our mission, to lead with prevention and intervention for substance use and mental health concerns, guides all agency programming. Our values of grit, integrity, and compassion are guideposts for all that we do in the service of our mission. Each staff member operates from these to ensure the success of the agency. PAS implements two statewide programs, Screening Brief Intervention, Referral to treatment (SBIRT), and the Peer Health Assistance Programs (PHAP)

**Screening, Brief, Intervention, and Referral to Treatment, or SBIRT,** is an evidence\-based early intervention practice to identify, reduce, and prevent use of alcohol and other substances. SBIRT calls for community\-based screening for health risk behaviors, including substance use. SBIRT in Colorado is a statewide program that provides training, technical assistance, and implementation support to health and mental healthcare providers, healthcare organizations, and stakeholders. SBIRT in Colorado manages a statewide campaign to increase public awareness of the risks related to alcohol, marijuana, and other drug use and to reduce the stigma of seeking treatment.

**Peer Health Assistance Programs** contract with the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies, Division of Professions and Occupations to provide the Peer Health Assistance Programs which are statutorily created and funded by license fees. These programs provide assessment, referral, long\-term case management and monitoring for health and mental health professionals with physical, emotional, psychiatric, psychological and/or substance use conditions affecting their practice.


These are the professions who have statutorily created programs for Nurses – RNs and LPNs, Direct Entry Midwives, Dentists and Dental Hygienists, Pharmacists and Pharmacy Interns, Veterinary Professionals, Marriage and Family Therapists, Professional Counselors, Psychologists, Social Workers, Addiction Counselors, and Unlicensed Psychotherapists.


The Peer Health Assistance Program is available on a fee for service basis to other licensed healthcare providers in Colorado who do not have a statutorily created program. These professions include physical therapists, surgical technicians/assistants, chiropractors, optometrists, nursing home administrators, podiatrists, athletic trainers, massage therapists, occupational therapists, respiratory therapists, and speech and language pathologists.  

Please visit our website at https://www.peerassistanceservices.org/ to learn more about the agency.

**About the Case Manager Position**


This is a hands\-on, full\-time position with day\-to\-day responsibilities that will include ensuring program participants are able to practice their profession with reasonable skill and safety, while complying with regulatory requirements. You will also collaborate with licensed evaluators to develop a monitoring contract outlining treatment and community resources to optimize program participants' physical and mental health and wellbeing. You will need to maintain regular communication with program participants, treatment providers, and workplace supervisors to measure compliance with the monitoring contract. You may also have to adjust monitoring contract requirements based on compliance measurements while keeping accurate records of contract monitoring throughout the program participant's involvement in the Peer Health Assistance Program. Your goal will be to help program participants achieve optimal health and well\-being while also meeting regulatory requirements.

**Compensation:** $55,000 to $60,000

**What will you do?**

* Provides comprehensive case management for Peer Health program participants.
* Comprehensive management of compliance with monitoring contracts.
* Collaborates with licensed clinical evaluators to provide referrals to treatment and other resources.
* Maintains accurate electronic participant records.
* Communicates with State Regulatory Boards.
* Directs participants to appropriate providers.
* Establishes and manages relationships with key partners, e.g., treatment and healthcare providers, employers, supervisors, and practice monitors.
* Conducts regular audits of program participants for quality assurance.
* Attends staff meetings including clinical consultation, office hours, case review, required trainings, and all agency meetings.
* Assists with additional program activities as requested.

**What education \& experience is required in this role?**

* Bachelor’s degree in a health and behavioral health\-related field, e.g., nursing, social work, or human services, is required.
* Two or more years of experience in case management is preferred.

**Do you have these special skills?**

* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Attention to detail and organization skills.
* Deliver high\-quality services to program participants and contracts.
* critical thinking

**Closing Date: applications are accepted on an ongoing basis**  

  

Colorado Residents: In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age\-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information. **What makes us different?**
